text:
maya: quick question — can we add a lightweight cost estimate field at ingest for traces so the live cost dashboard isn't blind for a few mins while billing backfills?

own: sounds useful. what's the accuracy target? do we want per-request USD estimate or just relative weight?

maya: per-request estimated micro-cost would be ideal (e.g. estimated_token_usd = 0.00012) so the dashboard can show near-real-time burn. not expecting perfect.

sasha: main gotcha is batching + KV cache reuse; an edge estimate will overcount if requests get merged or re-use cached tokens.

own: we could approximate by using model_config + provided token_hint + sequence_length_hint. cheap math at ingress.

lucas: example header we could accept from SDKs: `X-RDW-token-hint: 64` and `X-RDW-model: redwood-v1-7b` — proxy computes estimate.

maya: exactly. proposed envelope change: add `ingest_cost_estimate_microusd` in the trace envelope root. small numeric only.

noor: product note — even a 20-30% overestimate is fine if it's consistent; teams want visibility more than exact cents.

sasha: tradeoffs: 1) compute cost at edge (low latency, near-realtime), 2) compute later in ingestion (accurate after batching), 3) hybrid (edge hint + reconciliation).hybrid seems safest.

own: hybrid approach: add `ingest_cost_estimate` at ingress with an optional `batch_amortization_id` header if the request is enqueued for batching. billing pipeline can reconcile and write final `billing_cost` back to canonical record.

lucas: adding `batch_amort_id` means more metadata to persist in the queue. small, but ok. we should cap header sizes.

maya: operational flow I'd propose: 1) proxy computes estimate and tags trace envelope; 2) telemetry pipeline ingests envelope and emits near-real-time metrics keyed by `estimated`; 3) final billing enrich replaces/enriches with `billing_cost` and we emit delta metric to correct dashboards.

sasha: impl detail — make `ingest_cost_estimate` optional and always marked with `estimate_version` (e.g., "v1: model-factors+seq-hint"). that allows safe schema evolution.

own: also expose an explainable reason code: `estimate_reason: "seq_hint+model_default"` for debugging.

noor: can we show a flag in dashboard that toggles between "estimated" and "reconciled" cost? useful for product and sales demos.

maya: yes. dashboard teams will join.

lucas: security/PII check — estimates are numeric only, no customer-identifying info. fine for non-PHI pipelines. ensure privacy controls for private deployments.

sasha: perf note — edge CPU overhead: a few integer ops per request. add microbench and keep under 200ns per request path.

own: we should add unit tests that simulate batching to show expected overcount and reconciliation delta distribution.

maya: next steps: 1) small PoC in ingress proxy to compute estimate, push test traces to staging telemetry, 2) add estimate_version + reason fields to trace envelope schema, 3) reconciliation join key `batch_amortization_id` optional.

lucas: I can spin up a proxy branch this week. assigning to me. :thumbsup:

noor: I'll coordinate with dashboards to show estimated vs reconciled toggles.

sasha: I'll own the telemetry pipeline changes for emitting estimated metrics and delta reconciles.

own: doc ask — can someone add a short design note in the obs-infra docs explaining estimate math and known biases so product/finance understand.

maya: I'll draft the note and post in docs.

telemetry-bot: deploy-bot: staging proxy branch created: `ingest-cost-estimate/proxy-132` — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/proxy/pull/132

lucas: thanks, will push a microbench and sample traces shortly.

maya: awesome. if we hit weird edge cases we'll pause adoption, but this should give teams useful near-realtime visibility.

own: one more thought — we can add a small sampling label `estimate_confidence` (low/med/high) based on presence of seq hints and model metadata. cheap to compute and helps queries.

sasha: agreed. adds a lot of signal.

maya: cool, meeting-free follow-up. I'll post the short design note and link it here when ready. :sparkles:
